Short answer
- You remain responsible for fees that have "accrued through the effective date." Because termination for convenience requires 90 days' written notice, the effective date will (absent a different contract definition) be after that 90‑day notice period — so you would owe fees that accrue during and up to that effective date. Whether you owe anything beyond that (or are entitled to any refund for pre‑payments) depends on other contract provisions not shown here.

Exact clauses you gave (quote + citation you can paste into the memo)
- MSA, p.4, §3.2: "either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice."
- MSA, p.11, §7.1: "termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date."

Short explanation you can paste (one or two sentences)
- Per §3.2, termination for convenience requires 90 days' written notice; per §7.1, termination for convenience "does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date." Therefore, if Customer gives (valid) 90 days' notice, Customer remains liable for fees that accrue up to the termination effective date (i.e., through the end of the notice period unless the contract defines "effective date" otherwise).

Key uncertainties and risks to check before finalizing the memo
- Confirm how the contract defines "effective date" — it may be explicitly defined elsewhere and could alter timing.
- Search for any clauses on "accrued fees," refunds, credits, prepayments, or pro‑rata billing (these determine whether prepaid amounts are refundable or applied to the notice period).
- Check payment/invoice terms and any penalty or breach remedies if you stop without following the termination-for-convenience procedure (walking off immediately could be a breach with additional liability).
- Look for survival clauses or other sections that allocate post‑termination fees or costs.

Suggested next steps I can do for you
- If you paste the contract's definitions section and any payment/refund/prepayment, breach, or invoice clauses, I can locate and quote the relevant language and draft a short memo paragraph referencing the exact sections.
- Or I can draft a one‑paragraph memo containing the quotes and the interpretation above (with a short legal‑advice disclaimer) for circulation.

Note: I’m summarizing the clauses you provided, not giving legal advice — consider having in‑house or outside counsel review for a binding position.
